arguments.reasoning: Feedback first. The retained comparison fixed-radius (T0) reaches terminal 0.00313 m (F145) and holding position 0.00336 m (F284), both inside the 0.01 m bound, but holds at 0.02682 m/s (F28) above the 0.02 m/s bound; its holding_speed component fails (F13) so its status is valid_failure (F127). Its only binding deficiency is held tip speed. The only legal control-only levers here are exactly the two continuous recipe paths control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight and control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight, so speed-weight adaptation is the directly indicated intervention. The batch source must be distinct from both the latest tested entry (v2-T1) and the retained baseline (T0/fixed-radius). Of the remaining complete evidence, v2-T3 (holding speed 3.77 m/s, terminal 0.103 m) is dominated by v2-T2 on every recorded metric, so I branch from v2-T2. T2 is the four-segment template with the closest terminal error (F187 = 0.011093 m), a locally feasible controller-start input for position and braking (F567) and a locally feasible target equilibrium (F561), yet it still fails holding position (F1 = 0.023420 m), holding speed (F224 = 1.121 m/s) and acceptance (F192 = false, F3 = valid_failure) at the recorded nominal weights holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.05 (F497) and terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.1 (F354). A bounded coordinate search over those two recipe paths tests, under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, whether speed-weight adaptation alone can settle the hold window and shave the terminal error. Historical executions ran controller 9.0.0 (F323), so the v10 outcome is not certified by these numbers, hence the uncertain promise.
